chapter_theme: Taking the great as one's support (பெரியாரைத் துணைகோடல்): the poet resolves to keep company with those who run, sing, seek and join the Lord, bids his faltering heart come with him, and tells how, going with the devotees' devotees, he was announced at the Lord's gate and called in. Joining the great is supreme bliss.
structure_note: First-person resolve (543, 544), the general claim (545, 546), a short narrative of arrival (547) and a closing resolve (548).

543.reading: I will go along with those able to run to him and their kin; I will live on earth in the light of those able to sing; with the Lord of gods who grants grace to those able to seek, and with those able to join him, I will reach his feet.
543.nuance: வல்லார் (those able to) ends each verb: run, sing, seek, join. ஓட may also be 'to run away', from the world; the sense of eager devotion seems more likely.

544.reading: Though they suffer and tremble like tender leaves, they have set no love in the great mind there; O heart, what will you do, staying in distress? When I go, come with me.
544.nuance: The first two lines are obscure: it is not clear who suffers and whose mind is meant. The last two are an address to the heart, a device known from love poetry and the bhakti hymns.

545.reading: Seeking the Lord of the immortals, a few who draw near gain the reality; the great ones who stand ever more firmly in the path give grace, and to join with them is supreme bliss.
545.nuance: தத்துவம் (variant சிவதத்துவம்) here seems to mean the true reality rather than the 36 tattvas. பேரின்பம் is the bliss of release.

546.reading: Becoming in the world the kin of him whose matted hair bears a garland, praising him, they reach our father's golden feet; coming to the King who grants grace to those who search the heart without shutting the mouth, one can join that path.
546.nuance: வாயடையா உள்ளம் தேர்வார் is unclear: perhaps those who search their heart while still praising aloud. போர புகழா may be corrupt.

547.reading: I went with the devotees of the Lord's devotees and entered the city of him whose body is fire bearing weapons; those standing at the gate saw me and made me known, and the cry went up: 'The Lord says, let him come.'
547.nuance: The poet gains entry not alone but in the company of devotees of devotees, the humblest rank. ஓலம் is the call announcing an arrival or answering one.

548.reading: The one rare in skill appears in the knowledge of the arts; the one great in skill swims the whirlpool of births; the one with the rightful skill, understanding, abides for an aeon; I have joined those strong in holiness.
548.nuance: The verse plays on வல்லோன் with அருமை, பெருமை, உரிமை and திருமை. The variant ஞாலத்துள் for ஞானத்துள் would make the first line 'appears in the world of the arts'.

links.note: The Naladiyar's drain water that joins a great river becomes holy water, and the lowborn who join the good stand like a hill; Tirumular says joining the great is supreme bliss. Both make the company one joins transform the joiner.
The Kural calls cherishing the great and making them one's own the rarest of rare things; Tirumular's verse begins with அருமை and ends with 'I have joined those strong in holiness'.
543 resolves to go along with those who run to the Lord and reach his feet with them; 547 tells it happening, going with the devotees' devotees and being called in at the gate.

source_issues: 544: மாமனதது and இருநது, misprints for மாமனத்து and இருந்து.
546: தேர்வார்ககு, a misprint for தேர்வார்க்கு; போர புகழா may be corrupt.
548: variant ஞாலத்துள் for ஞானத்துள்; the verse ends with a doubled full stop.
